name: Turtlefolk
body:
Although native to a wide variety of warm and temperate climates, turtlefolk are reclusive and rarely feel the need to interact with others.

Physical

Turtlefolk look like humanoid turtles or tortoises. They have scaly skin, beak-like mouths, and webbed, claw-like hands that are surprisingly dexterous. Most significantly, they carry large shells on their backs, which provide them with both shelter and protection.

Social

Turtlefolk live in small communities, and usually subsist by hunting, farming, and fishing. They mostly live along coasts and rivers where food is plentiful, but can easily adapt to many other terrains. They are a quiet, peaceful folk.

Having their own shelter and fortress on their backs makes turtlefolk feel naturally self-sufficient, and this remains a primary motivation for most. They sometimes trade with other turtlefolk or humanoid communities, but they do not go out of their way to do so.

Alignment and Religion

Turtlefolk are known for their patience, wisdom, and generosity. They tend to be Lawful Good, although individual turtlefolk of every alignment exist.

Turtlefolk have no specific organized religion. Many communities have a patron nature deity or Empyreal Lord, but every citizens is free to adopt whatever deity they wish. Thanks to their long life and interest in learning, many turtlefolk supplement their faith with studies in philosophy, ethics, civics, and other studies.

Names

Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are strong and intuitive, but your reflexes are sluggish. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Wis, –2 Dex [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the reptilian subtype. (0)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. Your speed is never reduced by armor or encumbrance. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Turtlefolk. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aquan, Boggard, Draconic, Dwarven, Elven, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Species Traits
Armor Aversion Because of your bulky shell, you have a difficult time wearing armor, even if you have the appropriate feat. All armor is treated as being one class bulkier than normal for you: treat light armor as medium armor, and medium armor as heavy armor. You cannot wear heavy armor. Regardless of the kind of armor worn, you suffer an additional –2 armor check penalty, +10% arcane spell failure chance, and your maximum Dexterity bonus is reduced by 2 (to a minimum of 0). (–2)
Claws You have two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage each. (2)
Hold Breath You can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to 4 times your Constitution score before you risk drowning or suffocating. (1)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor Your hard shell provides you with a +3 natural armor bonus to AC. (5)
Resilient Swim and Survival are always class skills for you. (1)
Retract If you take the total defense action, you gain a +6 bonus to your Armor Class instead of the usual +4 bonus, and you also cannot be flanked until the start of your next turn. (2)
Total: 9 RP (standard)
Alternate Species Traits
Armor Adapted You have made adjustments to your shell, allowing you to more easily accommodate armor, but your natural armor bonus to AC is only +2. This trait alters natural armor and replaces armor aversion.
Burrower Your claws are specially adapted for digging. You gain a burrow speed of 10 feet. This trait replaces retract.
Cave Dweller You come from a long line of subterranean turtlefolk. You gain darkvision with a range of 60 feet. This trait replaces hold breath and low-light vision.
Desert Dweller You come from a hot, arid climate. When in conditions of severe heat, you have to attempt Fortitude saves only once per hour instead of once every 10 minutes. In addition, when you use your retract ability, you gain fire resistance 5. This trait replaces hold breath.
Hearty You gain a +2 bonus to Constitution instead of +2 Strength. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Professional You receive a +2 species bonus to one Craft or Profession skill of your choice. This trait replaces resilient.
Snapper You can use your beak to make a nasty bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. This trait replaces claws.
Student Choose any two Knowledge skills; once selected, these skills cannot be changed. These skills are always class skills for you. This trait replaces resilient.
Swimmer You have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. This trait replaces retract.
Species Feats
Shell Expert

You are an expert at using your shell to defend yourself.

Prerequisites: Retract species trait, Combat Reflexes.

Benefit: You can expend an attack of opportunity to parry an attack directed at you. You may declare the use of this ability after an attack roll or Reflex saving throw is made, but must do so before the results are revealed. If the attack required an attack roll, the attacker takes a penalty equal to you natural armor bonus; if the new result would be a miss, the attack is negated. If the attack was a ranged or area effect that included you as a target, you gain a bonus to your Reflex saving throw equal to your natural armor bonus; if the new result would be a success, your saving throw results in a reduced or negated effect, as specified in the effect’s description.

Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Reduce the amount of time you are fatigued after a rage by 1 round, to a minimum of 1 round.
Bard Add +1 to your total number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Cleric Add +1/3 to the amount of damage dealt or damage healed when you use channel energy.
Druid Add +1/3 to your natural armor bonus when using wild shape.
Fighter Add +1 to your melee attack roll when using the aid another action to help an ally either gain a bonus to their next attack roll or to their AC.
Kineticist Add +1/4 to your effective kineticist level for the purpose of determining the effects of your primary element’s defensive wild talent.
Monk Add +1/4 to your AC bonus monk class ability.
Oracle Add +1/4 to the armor or natural armor bonus granted by oracle spells you cast on yourself.
Paladin Add +1/2 hit point to your lay on hands ability (whether using it to heal or harm).
Ranger Increase your natural armor bonus to Armor Class by +1/4 against your favored enemies.
Rogue Add +1/4 to the number of times per day you can use the resiliency rogue talent or the defensive roll rogue talent. You must possess the associated rogue talent to select these options.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Spirit Warrior Add +1/5 to your spirit bonus when using the protection aura or shield aura.
Warpriest Add +1/2 to the number of times per day you can use blessings, but these additional uses can be from only the Animal, Earth, Flood, Plant, Protection, and Water blessings.
Witch Add +1/4 natural armor bonus to the AC of your familiar.
Wizard Add +1/3 to your effective caster level for wizard abjuration spells, but only to determine duration.
